script.text: A U.S. jet fired on a cargo ship leaving Iran. Can anyone break the blockade?

U.S. Central Command says one of its aircraft struck the stern of the Pacific Archer on Thursday in the Gulf of Oman. The Palau-flagged bulk carrier had sailed from Bandar Abbas and ignored repeated warnings, it says. The crew was unharmed.

The strike knocked out its propulsion. Central Command says one hundred fifty-eight other ships have turned back. By media counts, this is the sixth ship disabled since the blockade of Iranian ports resumed in July, and at least the fifteenth since April.

Iran's navy chief said breaking the blockade is underway, and that his orders are to keep Hormuz closed. Central Command says it controls the strait with partners. President Trump told troops victory will come whenever he wants it.
Will any ship break the U.S. blockade this year? Yes or no?

upload.title: US Jet Disables Ship Leaving Iran. Blockade Holds? #shorts
upload.description:
On Thursday, November 26, 2026 (Thanksgiving), a U.S. military aircraft fired a precision munition at the stern of the Palau-flagged bulk carrier M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman and disabled its propulsion, according to U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM). CENTCOM said the ship had sailed from Bandar Abbas, Iran, ignored repeated warnings while attempting to run the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports, and that the civilian crew was unharmed. CENTCOM did not allege that the ship took part in a ship-to-ship transfer; ship-tracking sites listed its destination as Singapore. The exact position of the strike was not disclosed; locations on the map are approximate. Some outlets described the vessel as a tanker or cargo ship; CENTCOM calls it a bulk carrier. CENTCOM says 158 other commercial vessels have complied and been redirected. According to media counts based on U.S. statements, the Pacific Archer is the sixth vessel disabled since the blockade resumed in July and at least the fifteenth publicly acknowledged since it began in April; counts differ between outlets. It is the first ship disabled since Iranian officials vowed to break the blockade (Iran International). Iran's navy commander, Rear Admiral Shahram Irani, said breaking through the blockade is underway and, per Al Mayadeen, that the orders are to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed; CENTCOM rejected his claims and says U.S. forces and regional partners control the strait. In Thanksgiving calls with deployed troops, President Trump said victory over Iran would come "whenever I want it to be" and that Tehran has every chance to make a deal. No Iranian official reaction to the Pacific Archer strike itself was found at the time of writing.
